page: Amazon Web Services r5ad.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a 2.5 GHz AMD EPYC 7571 processor delivering 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The instance provides 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features also include 1,200 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local instance storage and an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. There are no GPUs provisioned.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture oriented toward multi-threaded capacity and high-density memory workloads rather than single-threaded speed. In single-core tests, the r5ad.8xlarge posts lower-tier scores, including a Geekbench single-core result of 717.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 590.89. In contrast, multi-core benchmarks scale to mid-range performance, producing a PassMark CPU score of 22,216.79, Geekbench multi-core score of 6,127.0, and multi-core stress-ng metric of 9,443.73. Memory throughput measures 54.01 GB/sec for uncached read-only transfers and 26.41 GB/sec for uncached writes, enabling solid execution across caching systems, as evidenced by 19.58 million operations/sec in Redis SET operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the AMD-based configuration provides an economical path to acquiring substantial memory density alongside fast local NVMe storage. The architectural tradeoff centers on legacy single-thread latency and modest medium-model machine learning inference throughput, where the system manages 22.38 prompt tokens/sec and 6.45 text-generation tokens/sec on 7B models. These attributes position the r5ad.8xlarge specifically for in-memory databases, Redis caches, high-throughput database operations, ETL pipeline processing, and distributed memory-heavy enterprise deployments.

While single-thread benchmarks reflect lower relative processing power (Geekbench single-core 717.0), multi-core operations achieve consistent midrange ratings, marked by a PassMark CPU score of 22,216.79 and 19.58 million operations/sec in Redis SET tests.
